Your own widgets

A widget is defined in MKP's own small language, in an mkp fence. The fence draws nothing; any block in the document may use what it defines, before or after it.

```mkp
greeting "A line of welcome with a name in it."
  in name text = "world" "who to greet"
  text "Hello, **\val{name}**!"
  project md = "Hello, **" + name + "**!"
```

```greeting
name: reader
summary: A greeting for the reader.
```

One statement a line, children indented two spaces. The first line names the widget and says what it is for; then come its members, then what it draws, built from the base set.

#Members

In this order:

Member What it declares
in name type = default "about" An input, filled from the block's YAML. answer after the type marks one that holds the answer.
var name type = value The widget's own state.
name = slider 0..10 "label" State the reader changes with a control in the widget's bar: slider, toggle, choice(…), steps n, drag, clock.
name = expression A value worked out from what is above it.
fn name(x: num): num = expression A function, with its types written out.
out name {…} An event for the widget that uses this one (emit).
signal name {…} A message to the host app (send).
project md = expression The Markdown a reader without MKP gets instead.

Every widget you define needs a project md, unless it only holds content in a slot.

Controls can play themselves: steps 4 play=1s/step steps through on its own, and slider 0..1 play=8s loop=bounce sweeps back and forth.

#Expressions

Arithmetic, comparisons, and/or/not, if(c, a, b), lambdas x => …, and a library of built-ins for maths (sin, sqrt, round…), lists (map, filter, sum, range…), records and text (format, join, upper…). Writing two things side by side multiplies them, tighter than *: 2 pi k is , and 1/2x is .

Inside a string, \val{expr} shows a live value, in maths too: "$e^{\val{k}i}$".

#Events and actions

```mkp
tally "Counts the reader's clicks and tells the host."
  signal clicked {count: int}
  var n int = 0
  press
    text "Click me"
    @click set n=(n + 1) send clicked count=(n + 1)
  project md = "A button that counts clicks."
```

An event line (@click, @change, @submit, @enter, @leave…) runs actions in order: set, reveal and hide, play and pause, emit an event, send a signal. if=(…) on the line runs it only while it holds.

#Style by name

Style props take token names, never written-out values, so a host's theme decides how they look:

  • colours: surface ink muted line accent info ok warn bad, and c1–c6 for series
  • spaces: xs s m l xl, sizes s m l fill, fonts body heading mono
  • corners: card pill, shadow: raised

A colour such as #ff0000 is refused (mkp.style-token).

#Types

Inputs and values are typed: num, int, bool, text, color, list(T), records ({title: text, tone: color = muted}), choice(a|b|c) and more. A widget may take a type parameter, picklist of T, and read a field of each item through a path(T, text) input. The compiler checks every YAML value against its input's type, at its own line.

#Where definitions live

  • In the document, in an mkp fence: they belong to that document.
  • In name.mkp beside name.mkp.md: the same definitions, moved out.
  • In a pack: a folder with a manifest.mkp, its .mkp files, and fixtures that give every widget a valid case. A host loads it with --pack.

A name that a pack or the base set already gives is refused (mkp.shadow): copy the widget with a new name instead.

#Answers stay hidden

An input marked answer holds the answer to a question. A widget's Markdown may show it only inside if(answers, …), so mkp build --no-answers gives readers nothing away before they try (mkp.answer-leak otherwise). See it in the examples.
